chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: Crap games, the Ink Spots package and sandpapered dice
summary: Hinton and Francis trade stories of constant dice games; Bill Kinney of the Ink Spots kept Francis broke and his sanded dice backfired.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So I guess like all the bands, with Lucky's band and Lucky, that was quite a pastime for the boys, huh?
I remember in Cab Calloway's band, we shot dice, and I was one of the leaders, and I was always broke.
So was I! Don't you remember? They kept me broke.
I had the worst luck of any guy I ever met in my life.

No, I don't think so. I think I had the worst luck, because I'll tell you this story. We were traveling with the Ink Spots. The Ink Spots was owned by the same agency that owned Lucky's band, so we used to have a package -- and this package we had, Sister Thorpe, Peg Leg Bates, Timmie and Freddie, and the Ink Spots, and were in Lucky's Millinder's band. Well, the lead singer with the Ink Spots, Bill Kinney, [long] loved to gamble, and he had the idea that his loan money would always win, although I know of a couple of people who have bought homes off him -- and I was one of those that he kept broke all the time.
So, I had a cousin of mine that was living in Detroit and who was a professional gambler, and he took me one night to the Norwood Hotel.
In Detroit. Took me to the Norwood

Hotel, and got some fine sandpaper and some dice, just to show you how much bad luck I am, and he showed me how to sandpaper the dice down where it will make nothing but nine and five -- whenever you threw it out, you knew that nine out of ten times, you were going to make nine and five; the dice was stacked.

Do you know that I had sat up there all night sandpapering these dice, and the next day after the first show, we had a crap game in the dressing room -- and guess who got broke? Me. That's how bad my luck was.

Yeah, there were some really great crap games going on with all those bands, and word would be passed around from one band to another -- Lucky's band and Basie's band -- yeah, we'd pass the word around and tell about who would win the money and who was bad!

Yes. And then in each band, there was one guy that, although he played the music, he should have been a professional gambler, because he knew how to gamble and he was the one who used to win all the time. And each band had somebody like that.
